extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark for college-level multi-discipline multimodal understanding and reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines, 30 subjects, 183 subfields, and 30 heterogeneous image types to evaluate expert-level perception, knowledge, and reasoning in multimodal models.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue; Yuansheng Ni; Kai Zhang; Tianyu Zheng; Ruoqi Liu; Ge Zhang; Samuel Stevens; Dongfu Jiang; Weiming Ren; Yuxuan Sun; Cong Wei; Botao Yu; Ruibin Yuan; Renliang Sun; Ming Yin; Boyuan Zheng; Zhenzhu Yang; Yibo Liu; Wenhao Huang; Huan Sun; Yu Su; Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, and Wenhu Chen. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv:2311.16502, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was manually collected in three stages: the authors selected 30 subjects from common university majors, recruited over 50 university students specializing in those majors to collect multimodal questions, and had them gather questions from major textbooks and online resources while creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, and textbooks; major textbooks and online resources; free online resources, quizzes, textbooks, and other study materials; lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal college-level questions from textbooks, online resources, quizzes, and study materials, and create new questions where necessary; annotators were instructed to follow copyright and licensing rules, select questions without immediately available answers, ensure all questions contain one or more images, are in English, are college-level, unambiguous, and annotated with fields including question text, answer options, correct answer, image types, difficulty, and explanation; suspected duplicates were identified via lexical overlap and source URL similarity and reviewed by authors, problems were checked by co-authors for format and typos, and authors categorized difficulty levels and excluded about 10% of very easy problems.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: JSON file format; user-friendly web interface for data annotation and verification
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by the authors to eliminate duplications; a secondary review team rigorously vetted annotations, regular audits of random samples were conducted, ambiguities were flagged for detailed review in team meetings, and authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels and excluded approximately 10% classified as very easy.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: over 50 university students specializing in the selected majors; 30+ student annotators
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and “90th percentile of skilled adults,” nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle; the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Level 3, or Expert AGI, may lead to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption; We believe MMMU will stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The annotators should avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning; assess the expert-level multimodal understanding capability of foundation models across a broad scope of tasks; monitor the progress towards Expert AGI
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Version Change Log: CHANGES TO V2 (Dec.18) FROM V1 (Nov.27); CHANGES TO V3 (Dec.21) FROM V2 (Dec.18); CHANGES TO V4 (June.13) FROM V3 (Dec.21)
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking. This step requires authors to ensure adherence to a standardized format, undertaking necessary corrections where deviations are found.
